subject: chem
source: IB Diploma Programme Chemistry guide (first assessment 2025), HL (SL content + additional higher level) — Structure 1–3, Reactivity 1–3, tools, inquiry process and internal assessment

weeks.topic: Tools and inquiry: lab safety, measurement and uncertainty
objectives: Use common lab apparatus safely
Record measurements with uncertainties and significant figures
Distinguish random and systematic errors

weeks.topic: S1.1 Introduction to the particulate nature of matter
objectives: Classify matter as elements, compounds and mixtures
Describe changes of state with the kinetic model
Choose separation techniques for mixtures

weeks.topic: S1.2 The nuclear atom
objectives: Describe subatomic particles and atomic structure
Use nuclear symbols and isotopes
Calculate relative atomic mass from abundance
HL: Interpret mass spectra to find isotopic composition

weeks.topic: S1.3 Electron configurations
objectives: Interpret emission spectra and energy levels
Write electron configurations using s, p, d and f sublevels
Apply the Aufbau principle and Hund's rule
HL: Use successive ionisation energies and the convergence limit

weeks.topic: S1.4 Counting particles by mass: the mole
objectives: Use the Avogadro constant and molar mass
Determine empirical and molecular formulas
Calculate concentrations of solutions

weeks.topic: S1.5 Ideal gases
objectives: Describe the ideal gas model and its limits
Use the ideal gas equation pV = nRT
Calculate molar volume of gases

weeks.topic: R2.1 Stoichiometry: equations, limiting reactants and yield
objectives: Balance equations including state symbols
Identify the limiting reactant
Calculate theoretical and percentage yield and atom economy

weeks.topic: R2.1 Solutions: concentration and titration calculations
objectives: Calculate amounts in solution reactions
Perform acid–base titration calculations
Prepare standard solutions

weeks.topic: S2.1 The ionic model
objectives: Explain ionic bond formation
Deduce formulas of ionic compounds and polyatomic ions
Relate lattice structure to properties

weeks.topic: S2.2 Covalent model: Lewis structures, VSEPR and polarity
objectives: Draw Lewis formulas for molecules and ions
Predict shapes and bond angles with VSEPR
Determine bond and molecular polarity
HL: Use formal charge, resonance and expanded octets

weeks.topic: S2.2 Intermolecular forces, giant covalent structures and chromatography
objectives: Compare London, dipole–dipole forces and hydrogen bonding
Relate intermolecular forces to physical properties
Separate mixtures using chromatography
HL: Describe sigma and pi bonds and hybridisation

weeks.topic: S2.3–S2.4 Metallic bonding and from models to materials
objectives: Explain metallic bonding and properties of metals
Use the bonding triangle to classify materials
Describe alloys and addition polymers
HL: Relate transition metal d-electrons to metallic bonding

weeks.topic: S3.1 The periodic table: periodicity
objectives: Relate position in the table to electron configuration
Explain trends in atomic radius, ionisation energy and electronegativity
Describe acid–base character of oxides
Describe reactions of group 1 and group 17 elements

weeks.topic: S3.1 Transition elements and coloured complexes (HL)
objectives: Describe characteristic properties of transition elements
Explain variable oxidation states
Explain colour in complexes by d-orbital splitting

weeks.topic: Review: atomic structure, the mole and bonding
objectives: Consolidate atomic structure and electron configuration
Practise mole and stoichiometry calculations
Review bonding models
Consolidate HL ionisation energies and hybridisation

weeks.topic: R1.1 Measuring enthalpy changes
objectives: Distinguish exothermic and endothermic reactions
Calculate enthalpy change from calorimetry data
Draw energy profile diagrams

weeks.topic: R1.2 Energy cycles in reactions
objectives: Use bond enthalpies to estimate ΔH
Apply Hess's law
Construct energy cycles
HL: Use enthalpies of formation and Born–Haber cycles

weeks.topic: R1.3 Energy from fuels
objectives: Compare complete and incomplete combustion
Evaluate fossil fuels and biofuels
Describe fuel cells

weeks.topic: R1.4 Entropy and spontaneity (HL)
objectives: Explain entropy and predict entropy changes
Calculate ΔG = ΔH − TΔS
Predict spontaneity at different temperatures

weeks.topic: R2.2 Rates of reaction: collision theory and measurement
objectives: Define rate of reaction
Explain collision theory and activation energy
Measure rates by mass, gas volume or colour change

weeks.topic: R2.2 Factors affecting rate, Maxwell–Boltzmann and catalysts
objectives: Explain effects of temperature, concentration and surface area
Interpret Maxwell–Boltzmann distributions
Explain how catalysts work
HL: Determine rate equations, orders and the Arrhenius equation

weeks.topic: R2.3 Dynamic equilibrium and Le Châtelier's principle
objectives: Describe dynamic equilibrium in closed systems
Predict effects of changes using Le Châtelier's principle
Apply equilibrium ideas to industrial processes

weeks.topic: R2.3 Equilibrium constant Kc and reaction quotient Q
objectives: Write Kc expressions
Relate the size of Kc to equilibrium position
Compare Q with Kc to predict direction
HL: Solve equilibrium calculations and link Kc to ΔG

weeks.topic: S3.2 Functional groups and IUPAC nomenclature
objectives: Identify functional groups in organic molecules
Name compounds using IUPAC rules
Draw full, condensed and skeletal formulas

weeks.topic: S3.2 Homologous series and structural isomers
objectives: Describe trends in homologous series
Draw structural isomers
Classify primary, secondary and tertiary compounds
HL: Identify cis–trans and optical isomers

weeks.topic: Collaborative sciences project
objectives: Work in an interdisciplinary team on a real-world problem
Apply chemical knowledge to a shared investigation
Communicate and reflect on collaboration

weeks.topic: Mid-year exams: structure, energetics and kinetics
objectives: Sit Paper 1 and Paper 2 style questions
Apply calculations under timed conditions
Reflect on errors and timing
Include HL rate equations and entropy

weeks.topic: S3.2 Spectroscopic identification of organic compounds
objectives: Calculate index of hydrogen deficiency
Interpret IR spectra and mass spectra
Interpret ¹H NMR spectra
HL: Use splitting patterns and integration in ¹H NMR

weeks.topic: R3.1 Acids and bases: Brønsted–Lowry theory and pH
objectives: Identify conjugate acid–base pairs
Calculate pH from [H⁺]
Describe reactions of acids

weeks.topic: R3.1 Strong and weak acids and bases; the ionic product of water
objectives: Distinguish strong and weak acids and bases
Use Kw to relate [H⁺] and [OH⁻]
Compare conductivity and pH of strong and weak acids

weeks.topic: R3.1 Buffers, pKa, salt hydrolysis and pH curves (HL)
objectives: Calculate Ka, Kb, pKa and pKb
Explain buffer action and salt hydrolysis
Interpret pH curves and choose indicators

weeks.topic: R3.2 Redox: oxidation states and reactivity
objectives: Assign oxidation states
Write redox half-equations
Use the activity series of metals

weeks.topic: R3.2 Electrochemical cells: primary, secondary and fuel cells
objectives: Describe the operation of voltaic cells
Compare primary and secondary cells
Describe fuel cells
HL: Use standard electrode potentials to calculate cell potentials

weeks.topic: IA: exploring research questions
objectives: Generate focused, investigable research questions
Identify variables and suitable techniques
Review background chemistry

weeks.topic: IA: planning methodology and risk assessment
objectives: Design a method with sufficient, relevant data
Plan controls and repeat trials
Complete a safety, ethical and environmental assessment

weeks.topic: End-of-year exams: DP1 chemistry
objectives: Sit school exams covering DP1 topics
Use the data booklet accurately
Answer structured questions

weeks.topic: Review: DP1 reflection and IA preparation
objectives: Analyse exam performance by topic
Refine the IA research question
Plan preliminary trials
